title.narrative: Strengthening flood resilience in Nigeria to foster long-term societal stability – Focus on Niger State

description.narrative:
.Strengthening flood resilience in Nigeria to foster long-term societal stability – Focus on Niger State
This project is designed as a short-term, non-infrastructure intervention focused on strengthening flood preparedness, institutional coordination, and climate-informed decision-making in Niger State, with a particular focus on Mokwa Local Government Area. The intervention prioritizes capacity
Outcome 1: - Enhanced resilience and adaptive capacity in Niger State through strengthened institutional capacities and community preparedness for flood risk management, leading to reduced loss of life, protection of livelihoods and infrastructure, and improved investment decisions for long-term resilience.
Output 1.1: Community awareness and local capacity for flood preparedness strengthened. - Activity 1.1.1: Inception meeting at state and federal levels to formally launch the project, ensure stakeholder buy-in, and clarify institutional roles and coordination mechanisms. - Activity 1.1.2: Flood awareness campaigns conducted in flood-prone communities, including Mokwa and surrounding LGAs, using simple visual materials to communicate flood risks, early warning signals, and safe response measures, with particular attention to displaced youth and vulnerable groups. - Activity 1.1.3: Training of youth, teachers, and local volunteers as community focal points to support basic rainfall and river monitoring and to relay early warning messages through trusted local channels.
Verifiable outputs: One inception workshop conducted; awareness campaigns delivered; trained community focal points actively engaged
Output 1.2: Institutional coordination on flood early warning and preparedness strengthened. - Activity 1.2.1: Organization of one technical dialogue at state and national levels, bringing together relevant government agencies, technical institutions, the Ecological Project Office, development partners, and selected private sector actors to review recent flood impacts, identify preparedness and financing gaps, and agree on priority flood resilience actions. - Activity 1.2.2: Preparation of a concise, investment-oriented technical note outlining at least two priority flood resilience initiatives, designed to inform future funding decisions and partnerships.
Verifiable outputs: One multi-stakeholder technical dialogue conducted; one validated investment-oriented note produced
Output 1.3: Climate Risk–Informed Decision Analysis (CRIDA) conducted on a pilot basis and translated into actionable guidance. - Activity 1.3.1: Training of a core group of researchers and technical staff in Niger State on the CRIDA methodology and its application to flood risk management. - Activity 1.3.2: Application of the CRIDA methodology to assess past flood events, current exposure, and future climate risks in the Mokwa pilot area, with results synthesized into decision-relevant guidance for authorities. - Activity 1.3.3: Design and guidance for community-based demonstration activities on very low-cost, community-managed nature-based solutions—such as riverbank and floodplain vegetation restoration and vegetated buffer zones—aimed at reducing surface runoff and localized flood impacts.
Verifiable outputs: Trained CRIDA core team; completed pilot CRIDA analysis with actionable recommendations; implemented pilot nature-based solutions
TARGETS AND INDICATORS: By the end of the project, at least five communities and approximately 500 people will have enhanced flood preparedness awareness, with at least 40% women and 30% youth participation. One validated coordination and investment note will be produced. Up to 30 national experts will be trained on CRIDA, and one pilot CRIDA application will be completed in Mokwa.
